newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seita slips on smoker's suit.
newsitem.headline: Seita slips on smoker's suit.

text.p: Shares in tobacco group Seita, privatised last year, slipped on Thursday in a quiet market under the impact of negative publicity concerning a second civil suit in a week by the family of smokers who died.
At 1002 GMT, Seita was down 3.80 francs or 1.73 percent at 216.20 francs in a turnover of 996,081 francs.
Lawyer Francis Caballero told Reuters the suit was intended to force Seita to inform the public of the health risks of its products.

The latest suit, only the second legal case of its kind brought in France, was filed in the southern city of Beziers by the family of a young woman who died of lung cancer last October after smoking Gauloises Brunes cigarettes for over 20 years.
The suit said that Suzanne Berger of Servian, southern France, began smoking at the age of 13 and smoked 40 to 50 Brunes per day until she learned last year that she had cancer.
A Seita spokeswoman said the latest suit, like a similar complaint brought against the firm last week, lacked serious legal grounds.
She said similar suits filed outside France had never led to damages payments of any kind in the past.
Seita shares are coming back from a level of 225 francs reached on December 20 after a rise from 190 francs on November 19. It hit a year high of 243 francs on June 28.
